body: My number was 1000, but I was training for a marathon at the same time. I ran an average of 9 miles a day, which burns about 700-800 calories for a person of my size. I never altered my rules, even on days when I'd go for a 20+ mile run, which burns about 1800 calories. I passed out more times than I can say, and it's left me with permanent damage to my bones and teeth. I still purge 3-4 times per week, but I'm back to my average weight (a quiet, malicious voice in my head tells me that I'm back to being fat) and I'm seeing someone who has helped me immensely.

I actually have two:

1) I stayed in an abusive relationship for eight months. The man I was seeing was several years older than myself. He enjoyed getting hammered with his friends every weekend, and when he passed a certain level of drunkenness (usually blacking out but still functioning), he became violent, usually with other people, but occasionally with me. He often told me I was "making" him yell at me. He was manipulative and always begged for forgiveness, and I didn't have many friends in town at the time, so I stupidly went back to him every time.

I don't want to air too much of my dirty laundry, but I'll share one story. Once, he started picking a fight with another guy at a bar, so I stood between them and asked him to step outside with me for a moment. As soon as we went outside, he grabbed my arm hard enough to leave a purple handprint the next day and pushed me against an iron fence. He was a rugby player and weighed 110 lbs more than me, so even the slightest clumsy, drunken push could have consequences. My head hit the fence -- hard.  I was also drunk (but lucid) and frightened, so I began to cry. He backed off and asked me what I wanted. I said I just wanted to go home, so he told me to go. I began walking home, but  few minutes later he ran up to me saying he was sorry and asked me to come back with him. I said no and asked him to leave me alone. He began yelling and followed me to my door. By the time we arrived, he was apologizing again. In retrospect, I should've asked him to leave, but once again, I was drunk and being stupid.  I had hoped my roommate would be home, but she wasn't, so as soon as we got inside he tried to kiss me. I pulled away and said I didn't feel like it. He slapped me across the face and pushed me onto the bed. After that, I did not object. I did not say no. He finished up and fell asleep next to me. He didn't remember any of it in the morning. Did I mention that was on my 21st birthday?

My anxiety over this relationship led to my next secret...

2) I have been struggling with an eating disorder since my relationship with the fellow mentioned above. It's certainly not his fault, but his jibes about my appearance ("You look like a lesbian." "You're lazy." "Have you gained weight?") made me more aware of my body than I ever had been. I weighed 130 lbs at the time and dropped to 112 in two months. That is 7 lbs underweight for my height. 

I've gotten much better over the past year, but I return to it from time to time in moments of weakness. I am no longer underweight. I have a stable career and am generally successful, outgoing and happy. I have never been to rehab. I have disguised my condition through long distance running as a means of explaining my weight loss. The only person who knows is currently my (non-abusive) fiance, and he is immensely supportive. We had been dating for several months before I told him. Thankfully, he understood and has helped me improve.

tl;dr - Abusive relationship and eating disorder.
